angle_en: pranasyaami: the promise of never being lost
angle_hi: प्रणश्यामि: कभी न खोने का आश्वासन

en.intro: What happens to a person who truly sees the divine in every living thing? Krishna answers with a promise of unbreakable closeness.
en.notice: The word pranasyaami means to disappear or be lost. Krishna says he will never disappear from the yogi's sight, and the yogi will never disappear from his.
en.next: Krishna then says this united yogi lives in him and acts in the world without losing that vision. Listen to verse thirty-one.
en.meaning: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me.

hi.intro: जो व्यक्ति हर जीवित प्राणी में ईश्वर को सचमुच देखता है, उसका क्या होता है? श्रीकृष्ण इसके बारे में एक अटूट निकटता का आश्वासन देते हैं।
hi.meaning: जो सबमें मुझे देखता है और सबको मुझमें देखता है, उसके लिए मैं कभी अदृश्य नहीं होता और वह मेरे लिए कभी अदृश्य नहीं होता।
hi.notice: प्रणश्यामि शब्द का अर्थ है लुप्त होना या खो जाना। श्रीकृष्ण कहते हैं कि वह कभी भी उस योगी की दृष्टि से लुप्त नहीं होंगे और वह योगी भी कभी उनकी दृष्टि से लुप्त नहीं होगा।
hi.next: इसके बाद श्रीकृष्ण कहते हैं कि ऐसा एकजुट योगी उनमें स्थित होकर भी संसार में कर्म करता है।

en.intro: What happens to a person who truly sees the divine in every living thing? Krishna answers with a promise of unbreakable closeness.
en.body: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me. The word pranasyaami means to disappear or be lost. Krishna says he will never disappear from the yogi's sight, and the yogi will never disappear from his. Krishna then says this united yogi lives in him and acts in the world without losing that vision. Listen to verse thirty-one.

issues: meaning_changed: "मैं कभी अदृश्य नहीं होता" (The Hindi meaning uses 'अदृश्य' (invisible), but the original Sanskrit 'प्रणश्यामि' means 'am lost' (प्रणश्यामि = प्र + नश् = to be lost). The Hindi translation drops the core meaning of 'being lost' and replaces it with 'being invisible', which significantly changes the meaning of the verse.)
